requirement:
`Criterion::execute` can compute an answer without a configured model provider.
A criterion can compute its answer directly using tracked inputs; deterministic
execution needs no configured agent.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.sdk.graph.criteria.deterministic_procedures` has no implementation roots, and none are needed. The text has two clauses: "`Criterion::execute` can compute an answer without a configured model provider" and "deterministic execution needs no configured agent". Both are capability statements about observable behavior. A criterion whose `execute` only reads tracked inputs through the context must complete and return its answer when no provider or agent is configured.

The text names no library, algorithm, type, field or delegation interface. The only candidate structural point is that `Criterion::execute` takes no provider parameter. In `crates/trust-but-verify/src/graph.rs#trait[Criterion]/fn[execute]` it takes only `self` and `ctx: &mut ValidationContext`. I treat that as an observable property rather than a prescribed signature.

The text does not require that exact declaration. A different declaration, such as one taking an optional agent argument, would still satisfy it if deterministic criteria still run with no agent. Conversely, a declaration that took a provider but failed without one would fail on behavior. A test would catch that failure, so the obligation needs no `{impl}` marker.

Code such as `Validator::execute` in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/graph.rs`, which takes `Option<&dyn Agent>`, only produces the required behavior. Finding it does not create a structural obligation. Whether tests verify this behavior belongs to the behavioral criterion.

behavioral: The requirement `requirements.sdk.graph.criteria.deterministic_procedures` has two behavioral obligations. First, `Criterion::execute` can compute an answer with no configured model provider. Second, a criterion can compute its answer directly from tracked inputs, without needing an agent.

- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[deterministic_validation_uses_required_storage_without_an_agent]` is the main test. It uses a `Memory` domain with no agent. It asserts that `ValidationContext::ask::<bool>` returns `NoAgentConfigured`, which shows no agent is available. It then runs `validator.verify(Review(..))` and gets `result == false` with rationale "ordinary computation". The stored evidence has a `Dependency::Node` whose fingerprint is "ordinary computation", so the answer was computed from a tracked input.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/configured.rs#mod[tests]/fn[configured_agents_initialize_only_when_asked_and_report_setup_errors]` uses a domain whose agent config has a missing credential. A deterministic `Question(false, ..)` still succeeds, with output false and one dependency. Only the question that asks the agent fails, with a `Provider` error. So a configured but unusable agent does not affect deterministic execution.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/graph/validation_tests.rs#fn[caller_reuses_negative_answers_and_compares_revisions_explicitly]` and `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/contracts.rs#fn[criteria_keep_typed_answers_and_persist_only_when_requested]` also run deterministic criteria through `verify`. They assert the computed outputs, the dependencies (empty or tracked), the execution counts, and that no agent is needed.

Together these tests cover both obligations: execution without an agent, and computing from tracked inputs. I found no gap.
